subject: ss-cardiology
title: Chronic coronary syndromes: clinical evaluation, medical therapy and revascularization

steps.tx: **Typical angina** pectoris requires satisfying 3 diagnostic criteria: substernal chest discomfort of characteristic quality and duration, provoked by physical exertion or emotional stress, and relieved by rest or sublingual nitroglycerin within minutes. Atypical angina meets 2 criteria, while non-anginal chest pain meets only 1 or none.
steps.say: Typical angina pectoris requires satisfying three clinical criteria. First, substernal chest discomfort of characteristic quality and duration. Second, provocation by physical exertion or emotional stress. Third, prompt relief by rest or sublingual nitroglycerin within minutes. Meeting two criteria defines atypical angina, while meeting one or none defines nonanginal pain.

steps.tx: The landmark **ISCHEMIA trial** demonstrated that among patients with stable chronic coronary disease and moderate-to-severe ischemia on stress testing, routine invasive revascularization did not reduce all-cause mortality or major ischemic cardiovascular events compared to optimal medical therapy alone. Revascularization improved quality of life and angina frequency in symptomatic patients.
steps.say: The landmark ISCHEMIA trial demonstrated that in stable chronic coronary syndromes with moderate to severe stress ischemia, an initial invasive revascularization strategy did not reduce death or ischemic cardiovascular events compared to optimal medical therapy. Catheterization provided substantial symptom relief and quality of life benefits in patients with frequent angina.

left.title: Invasive Strategy
points: Routine coronary angiography and revascularization with optimal medical therapy; superior angina relief.

right.title: Conservative Strategy
points: Optimal medical therapy alone; invasive evaluation reserved strictly for refractory symptoms or acute syndromes.

steps.tx: **First-line antianginal** medical therapy comprises beta-blockers and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers to reduce myocardial oxygen consumption. Beta-blockers blunt resting and exercise heart rates, lower systemic arterial blood pressure, and depress contractility. Dihydropyridines such as amlodipine are combined when angina persists despite titrated beta-blocker dosing.
steps.say: First line antianginal pharmacotherapy comprises beta blockers and calcium channel blockers to decrease myocardial oxygen consumption. Beta blockers blunt resting and exercise heart rate, lower systemic blood pressure, and diminish myocardial contractility. Amlodipine is combined when symptoms persist despite target beta blocker dose titration.

steps.tx: **Ranolazine** provides antianginal efficacy without lowering heart rate or arterial blood pressure by selectively inhibiting the late inward sodium current in ischemic cardiomyocytes. Attenuating late sodium entry prevents intracellular sodium accumulation, reversing reverse-mode sodium-calcium exchange and reducing diastolic calcium overload to improve microvascular myocardial relaxation.
steps.say: Ranolazine provides antianginal efficacy without affecting heart rate or blood pressure by selectively inhibiting late inward sodium current in ischemic cardiomyocytes. Attenuating excess late sodium entry halts reverse mode sodium calcium exchange, preventing diastolic calcium overload and improving left ventricular relaxation and microvascular perfusion.

steps.tx: The membrane diagram shows **ranolazine** blocking the late inward **sodium current** through Nav1.5 channels during ischemia. Less sodium entry prevents intracellular **sodium overload** and stops reverse mode **sodium calcium exchange** from loading the cell with calcium. Lower diastolic calcium eases stiffness and wall tension so relaxation and microvascular flow improve without changing heart rate.
steps.say: This diagram shows how ranolazine relieves angina without slowing the pulse. It blocks late sodium entry through the heart sodium channel. With less sodium inside, the exchanger no longer runs backward and calcium no longer builds up in diastole. Less calcium means lower wall tension and better relaxation and blood flow in tiny vessels.

vis.alt: Membrane view showing blocked sodium channel plus calmed exchanger plus eased calcium load.
vis.caption: Diagram of blocked late sodium entry easing calcium load and wall tension, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Nicorandil** exerts dual-mechanism coronary antianginal actions by combining nitrate-like organic venodilation with opening of ATP-sensitive potassium channels in resistance arterioles. Nitrate actions reduce ventricular preload, while vascular potassium channel opening Hyperpolarizes vascular smooth muscle membranes, inducing profound epicardial and microvascular coronary arterial dilation.
steps.say: Nicorandil exerts dual mechanism coronary antianginal actions by combining nitrate-like venodilation with opening of adenosine triphosphate sensitive potassium channels in resistance arterioles. Nitrate venodilation reduces preload, while potassium channel opening hyperpolarizes smooth muscle to promote systemic and coronary arterial vasodilation.

steps.tx: **Ivabradine** selectively inhibits hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels carrying the funny current in the sinoatrial node. Slowing spontaneous diastolic depolarization decelerates heart rate in patients in normal sinus rhythm with baseline rate >= 70 bpm without depressing ventricular contractility, conduction velocity, or systemic vascular resistance.
steps.say: Ivabradine selectively inhibits hyperpolarization activated cyclic nucleotide gated channels that mediate the funny current in sinoatrial nodal pacemaker cells. Decelerating spontaneous diastolic depolarization lowers heart rate in patients in sinus rhythm without altering ventricular contractility, atrioventricular conduction, or arterial blood pressure.

left.title: Ivabradine Mechanism
points: Pure If current blockade in SA node; heart rate reduction with zero negative inotropy or bronchospasm.

right.title: Beta-Blocker Mechanism
points: Beta-1 adrenergic receptor blockade; reduces heart rate, contractility, blood pressure, and AV conduction.

steps.tx: **INOCA** encompasses ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries driven by coronary microvascular dysfunction and epicardial vasospasm. Diagnostic confirmation requires coronary reactivity testing in the catheterization laboratory. Intracoronary acetylcholine administration assesses endothelium-dependent microvascular dilation and reproduces vasospastic angina, while adenosine measures coronary flow reserve.
steps.say: Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries, termed INOCA, comprises coronary microvascular dysfunction and epicardial vasospastic disorders. Invasive diagnostic confirmation requires coronary reactivity testing with intracoronary acetylcholine and adenosine to measure coronary flow reserve and document reproduction of ischemic symptoms and epicardial spasm.

steps.tx: The baseline panel shows a widely patent LAD labelled **nonobstructive coronary arteries** with brisk distal flow. After intracoronary **acetylcholine administration**, the same LAD develops diffuse **epicardial spasm** with distal **microvascular slow flow**. The inset shows restored calibre after nitroglycerin. Because spasm reproduces ischaemia without fixed stenosis, provocation testing directs calcium channel and nitrate therapy rather than stenting.
steps.say: The paired angiograms show a normal baseline LAD that narrows diffusely after acetylcholine, with sluggish distal flow, then opens again after nitroglycerin in the inset. This reversible spasm explains ischaemia without fixed blockage, so documenting it matters because it points treatment toward vasodilator medicines instead of a stent.

vis.alt: Paired coronary angiograms showing baseline patent LAD with acetylcholine induced diffuse spasm and nitroglycerin reversibility inset.
vis.caption: Acetylcholine provocation showing reversible coronary spasm, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Trimetazidine** acts as an antianginal metabolic modulator by selectively inhibiting mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase, the terminal enzyme of fatty acid beta-oxidation. Shifting myocardial energy metabolism away from oxygen-demanding fatty acid oxidation toward glucose oxidation preserves ATP generation and protects intracellular homeostasis during acute myocardial ischemia.
steps.say: Trimetazidine functions as a metabolic antianginal modulator by selectively inhibiting mitochondrial 3 ketoacyl coenzyme A thiolase, the final enzyme of fatty acid beta oxidation. Suppressing fatty acid oxidation shifts myocardial metabolism toward glucose oxidation, generating more adenosine triphosphate per mole of oxygen consumed during ischemia.
